transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-27
Start: 15:30 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Sentry Head of Security), Tommy Li (Sentry Platform Lead), Rachel O'Neill (Sentry CTO)
Shared artifacts: Sentry pre-call questionnaire (link in chat), Redwood SOC2 summary (to be shared), SAML integration guide (redwood.docs/sso/saml)

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey, thanks everyone for joining, appreciate you squeezing this in. quick intros?
[00:08] Aisha Khan: yeah hi, im aisha, head of security at Sentry Systems, i've got tommy our platform lead and rachel our cto on. we're mainly here to understand security posture across hosted vs dedicated vs private.
[00:20] Diego Alvarez: great, i'm diego, se on redwood, i focus on infra and private deployments. i'll dig into encryption and audit logging details.
[00:27] Rachel O'Neill: thanks, we'll try to be frank about constraints — we handle PHI-adjacent telemetry so data residency and encryption are big.

Summary / Goals (auto):
- Confirm Redwood's compliance artifacts (SOC2, ISO) and support for SSO/SAML and RBAC.
- Understand KMS/BYOK options, audit log retention and export, and private deployment network models.
- Decide next steps for POC type (hosted sandbox vs dedicated pilot).

Topics noted: SOC2/ISO artifacts, SSO (SAML/OIDC), RBAC roles, audit logs and retention windows, encryption at rest (customer KMS), VPC/private control plane, data deletion / retention policy, dedicated performance sizing.

Transcript Body:
[00:45] Maya Chen: to start, what's your current stack for identity and key management? are you using a third-party IdP and a cloud KMS?
[00:52] Tommy Li: we use Okta for SSO, SAML, and AWS KMS with a combination of AWS-managed CMKs and customer-managed CMKs for sensitive stores. but for any PHI we want the keys to be fully customer-controlled.
[01:05] Aisha Khan: and compliance-wise, we need both SOC2 type II and ISO 27001 evidence for our vendors. we also need audit logs shipped to our SIEM and retention for at least 2 years.
[01:16] Diego Alvarez: understood. Redwood's hosted offering has SOC2 Type II and we're ISO-aligned — we can share the SOC2 report under an NDA, and we have an ISO 27001 summary as well. for KMS, hosted supports bring-your-own-key patterns via customer KMS integrations and we also offer Dedicated and Private where you keep full control.
[01:34] Rachel O'Neill: when you say BYOK for hosted, how does that work? do you hold any plaintext or is it envelope encryption?
[01:40] Diego Alvarez: good question. hosted uses envelope encryption by default: model payloads are encrypted in transit with TLS, then at rest with service keys. for BYOK we support envelope keys where the data encryption key is wrapped by your CMK — Redwood never persists your unwrapped DEKs. you can choose customer-managed keys in AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or Azure Key Vault. there is also an HSM-backed option for Dedicated/Private.
[02:05] Tommy Li: any limitations on key rotation or access logs for the KMS calls? we need to see every Decrypt/Encrypt call in our logs.
[02:12] Diego Alvarez: KMS call logs are visible in your cloud audit logs. for Dedicated/Private we can stream logs directly to a customer-controlled logging endpoint (S3, Cloud Storage, or SIEM ingest). hosted can also ship audit events to your SIEM via push, but there is a short buffer window — we'll send the events in near real time.
[02:31] Aisha Khan: what about RBAC? we need fine-grained roles so ops can't call sensitive endpoints, and separate roles for billing vs infra.
[02:39] Maya Chen: Redwood supports org-level RBAC with role templates — admin, dev, audit, billing — and custom roles via our console. for Private deployments you can also sync via SCIM to your IdP for group membership mapping.
[02:53] Tommy Li: do service-to-service calls support mTLS inside a VPC?
[02:56] Diego Alvarez: yes for Private we support mTLS between components and can run entirely inside your VPC with no egress to our hosted control plane if you choose the air-gapped option. for Dedicated you get customer-dedicated GPU pools plus a private control plane path option.

[03:18] Rachel O'Neill: audit logs — what events are captured and what's the retention granularity? we need creation, delete, key use, model rollout changes, API calls with token origin, and ideally prompt-level metadata for forensics.
[03:30] Diego Alvarez: we capture API calls, model version rollouts, route changes, key operations (wrapped/unwrap events), and token-level metadata like token id, route, and latency. prompt-level data is captured only if you enable request logging — by default we store minimal telemetry. retention is configurable: hosted default is 90 days, but under enterprise plans we can extend to 365 days or ship to your long-term store for 2+ years.
[03:58] Aisha Khan: shipping logs to our SIEM is a hard requirement — we can't rely on a vendor-only retention window. can Redwood push to our S3 bucket or Splunk?
[04:05] Maya Chen: yes, we support pushing logs to S3 or Cloud Storage and have connectors for Splunk/Datadog. for very sensitive logs we recommend shipping raw events to customer buckets where you manage lifecycle policies.
[04:18] Tommy Li: latency concerns: if we enable customer-side encryption and log shipping, does that add significant tail latency to inference?
[04:25] Diego Alvarez: encryption is async at rest; it doesn't affect per-request latency in a measurable way. log shipping is batched and usually won't impact tails, but if you enable synchronous request-level logging (you're awaiting a log ack) that could add latency — we generally avoid sync logging on the hot path.
[04:44] Rachel O'Neill: on the compliance front, will Redwood allow an on-site audit or provide SOC2 bridge letters?
[04:49] Maya Chen: we provide SOC2 reports under NDA and can provide a bridge letter for recent changes. on-site audits for hosted are rare, but for Private/on-prem we can accommodate more detailed audits through our enterprise support contracts.

[05:05] Aisha Khan: data deletion and retention — we need proof that data used in model ops is deleted on request and that backups are purged. what's Redwood's deletion SLA?
[05:14] Diego Alvarez: we have deletion workflow that triggers deletion across primary and backup stores; for hosted the deletion propagation is up to 72 hours in general, enterprise SLA can be faster. for Dedicated/Private you control the backups and deletion policies. we can produce deletion receipts and audit entries showing the delete events.
[05:32] Tommy Li: does Redwood ever use customer data to fine-tune models?
[05:36] Maya Chen: no — by default we do not train on customer data. we can sign contraints in the contract; hosted default is no training, and for ent plans we explicitly guarantee data isolation.

[05:46] Aisha Khan: SAML specifics: mapping group attributes to RBAC roles and SCIM provisioning — how mature is your connector?
[05:54] Diego Alvarez: our SAML connector supports attribute mapping for groups and roles; SCIM provisioning is supported for user sync and group membership. we have docs and a sample IdP config; I'll share a SAML guide link after the call.
[06:06] Rachel O'Neill: backup encryption — are snapshots encrypted with the same KMS? how are keys rotated?
[06:12] Diego Alvarez: snapshots are encrypted with the same CMK when using customer-managed keys. key rotation is supported and does a rewrap process; there is an automated rotation flow for service-managed keys. for BYOK we leave rotation control to you and provide mechanisms to rewrap prior DEKs.

[06:28] Maya Chen: quick qualification: how urgent is this — are you evaluating now for a platform choice, or is this long-term?
[06:34] Tommy Li: timeline is tight — we'd like to pick a vendor and kick off a pilot in Q3; security sign-off is a gating item, so getting SOC2 and KMS details accelerated is important.
[06:43] Aisha Khan: also, we need to know about breach notification SLA and support for forensic exports if asked by regulators.
[06:50] Diego Alvarez: we have breach notification in our security policy — we notify customers within 72 hours of detection and provide forensic logs; for enterprise contracts we can shorten that window and provide a runbook for incident response.

[07:03] Rachel O'Neill: are there any compatibility issues with our model artifacts? we run a trimmed LLM and rely on KV cache semantics. any issues with quantized models?
[07:12] Diego Alvarez: the runtime supports multiple quantization formats and KV cache persistence; for Dedicated we can pin kernel selection and sequence length configs. we'll need a short benchmark to validate your exact model and sequence lengths — we recommend a 1-day perf test on a dedicated lane.

[07:26] Maya Chen: competitors — any specific red flags we should know about?
[07:29] Aisha Khan: we've kicked some tires with CloudAI Endpoints and IncisiveOps; IncisiveOps was solid but lacked BYOK options for hosted. CloudAI's logs were slow to export.

[07:40] Diego Alvarez: that's helpful. for visibility, we can show token-level billing and latency breakdowns in the console, plus trace hooks to tie calls back to your request ids.

[07:50] (brief cross-talk, background noise)
[08:00] Tommy Li: real quick — network model for private: is the control plane still hosted? we want a private control plane or at least a private connectivity option.
[08:08] Diego Alvarez: two options: Private (customer-run control plane) which lives in your VPC/on-prem, or Dedicated with private connectivity where the control plane is logically separated and we provide an IP-sec/VPN peering. Private gives you the most control; Dedicated is faster to stand up.

[08:27] Aisha Khan: for auditability, can you produce immutable logs with append-only hashes? we prefer logs that we can attest haven't been tampered with.
[08:34] Diego Alvarez: we can provide signed audit logs and chain-of-custody metadata for enterprise accounts — that's part of our higher tier. alternatively shipping logs immediately to your bucket gives you independent custody.

[08:50] Maya Chen: let's surface decision criteria — what must happen for you to choose hosted vs dedicated vs private?
[08:58] Rachel O'Neill: in order: 1) proof of SOC2/ISO and KMS patterns, 2) ability to ship audit logs to our SIEM for two-year retention, 3) BYOK and key control (no vendor-side decryption), 4) acceptable latency for inference under our 50ms p50 target. If hosted meets all but key-control, we lean Dedicated. If hosted meets BYOK and log shipping to our bucket, we might pilot hosted first.

[09:26] Diego Alvarez: noted. for the latency target, we should run a short perf test on your representative prompts and payload sizes; Dedicated can usually meet tighter tails because of isolation.

[09:40] Maya Chen: ok, recap and next steps. I'll send a follow-up email and attach SOC2 artifacts. diego will coordinate a deep technical session and perf testing. tommy will share the PHI scope and IdP/KMS vendors.

[09:56] Aisha Khan: sounds good. one more question: retention of prompts — can we redact or exclude prompt text from logs?
[10:03] Diego Alvarez: yes, we support field-level redaction and tokenization before logging. you can configure to omit prompt bodies and keep only metadata.

[10:15] Rachel O'Neill: and pricing visibility — can you give an estimate for Dedicated entry price (monthly) for our scale? we run about 800 qps peak internal, 50 qps external, approximate.
[10:24] Maya Chen: we'll produce a sizing + cost estimate as part of the deep-dive artifacts; diego will include batch sizes and quantization options that materially change cost.

[10:36] (wrap-up)
[10:38] Maya Chen: ok thanks everyone — we'll get the artifacts over. expected timing, maya sends SOC2 by 06/01, diego schedules deep-dive early next week, tommy shares scope by end of the week.
[10:50] Tommy Li: thanks, talk soon.
[10:52] Aisha Khan: thanks all.

Meeting close: 16:12 PDT
